Maria P.: Quick idea — instead of long blanket 72h soaks for every flagged card, what if we move to a probabilistic sampling + micro-soak pipeline?
Lee W.: Curious, explain the "probabilistic" part. How do we pick cards to fully soak vs quick-check?
Maria P.: Stratified sampling. Priority slots: recent Xid/ECC counts, thermal anomalies, and age. We run an intensive micro-soak (6–12h) on a random subset within each stratum. If failures surface, escalate to full soak + detailed diag. If not, we mark as low-risk and put back in pool with a short-ttl quarantine.
Sam K.: That would save GPU hours. What's the failure detection criteria during micro-soak? Single Xid? thermal spike?
Maria P.: Proposed signals: any Xid >= 1 with reproducible stack, ECC-corrected rate > baseline, weird power cycling, or kernel oops. Also persistent repro across two micro-soak runs. We should tune thresholds to match historical post-return failure rates.
Jit P.: Implementation detail: micro-soak harness should run synthetic kernels + model-ish traces. e.g. random long sequences, KV cache warmups, and memstress. Repro script can be: `./diag-run --profile model-trace --duration 6h --log /tmp/soak.log`.
OpsBot: automated note: queued 12 GPUs for micro-soak (rack-g4-03: slots 2,5,6; rack-g3-07: slot 1; region: us-west2). ETA 6h.
Ashley R.: How do we avoid impacting capacity for high-throughput clusters? We can't pull many nodes during weekday peak.
Maria P.: Two mitigations: 1) schedule micro-soaks to run on low-priority capacity windows (nights + weekends) and on dedicated quarantine pools, 2) use sampling fraction that keeps expected withdrawn capacity < 1% of pool.
Lee W.: For evacuation policy: if micro-soak finds a flake, do we auto-drain + replace or require manual triage?
Maria P.: Auto-drain to isolation pool + trigger a hardware diagnostic job. Human-oncall gets a notification to approve RMA if the hw diag fails reproducibly. Auto-RMA only if we have a clear signature (e.g., persistent Xid pattern + thermocycle repro + failing memtest).
Sam K.: Don't forget driver/kernel pinning in repro — we've seen flakes only under a particular driver build. Add a test matrix: latest + pinned stable.
Jit P.: Agree. Also capture `nvidia-smi -q`, `dmesg | grep -i xid`, `sudo journalctl -u nv-hostengine` at 1m intervals during soak. Small log snippet idea:
```
[00:14:22] GPU0 ECC 5 correctable errors
[01:02:10] Xid 31 on GPU0: pcie link reset
[01:02:12] kernel: nvidia: GPU has fallen off the bus
```
Maria P.: Good logs. We should centralize logs in the `gpu-soak` index with tags: serial, host, rack, driver, probe-profile.
Ashley R.: Cost tradeoff: estimate — current blanket 72h policy uses ~9k GPU-hours/month. With sampling + micro-soaks we'd expect ~40% reduction while keeping post-return failure rate within 1.5x of baseline. Need to validate with A/B for a month.
Lee W.: A/B plan: pick two similar pools for 30 days, measure returns flagged within 14 days and emergency RMAs. Also measure latency/capacity impact.
Maria P.: I'll draft an experiment plan + configs for the harness and the telemetry dashboard. Will stub the job spec like:
```
name: micro-soak-v1
duration: 8h
profile: mixed-trace
signals: xid,ecc,temp,power
es_index: gpu-soak
```
Sam K.: If you want, I can hook up the job runner and add a rollout flag so we can flip on sampling fraction easily.
Maria P.: Awesome — assign to Sam for infra, Jit for diag scripts, Ashley to own cost/metrics. I'll own experiment plan and oncall playbook. I'll post PR for the harness configs tomorrow.
OpsBot: reaction :thumbsup:
Maria P.: Thanks — we'll iterate. If anyone has historical failure curves by age/slot/driver, please drop links here.
Ashley R.: Dropping link to internal sheet: https://redwood.internal/ops/gpu-failures/sampling-baseline (perm: eng-infra)
Lee W.: I'll pull driver-specific failure histogram and post by EOD.
Maria P.: Great — meeting cadence: 15m sync Fri to review initial micro-soak results next week.
